title: Raise All But One
statement:
You get an integer array nums of length n. In one move you pick any n − 1 of the elements and add 1 to each of them. The element you leave out stays the same.

Return the minimum number of moves needed to make all elements equal. It is always possible.

examples.why: Raising everything except one element is the same as lowering just that element, relative to the rest. The 5 must come down by 3 and the 3 by 1: 4 moves.
Each move raises the smaller one by 1. Negatives work the same way.

constraints: The answer fits in a 64-bit signed integer (and in a JS number)
hints: Try a tiny case by hand, like [1, 3]. Which element should you leave out each time?
Adding 1 to everyone except x changes all the differences exactly like subtracting 1 from x alone. Only the differences matter for "all equal".
So the question becomes: how many single-element decrements bring everything down to the minimum? That is the sum of nums[i] − min.

explain.intuition:
Whether the elements are equal depends only on their differences, not on their absolute level. Raising n − 1 elements by 1 changes every difference exactly as lowering the one left-out element by 1 would. So the move is really "lower one element by 1".

With that view the answer is easy. Lowering never helps the smallest element, and every other element must come down to it. The total number of moves is Σ (nums[i] − min) = sum − n · min. You can't do better, since each move closes only one unit of one gap.
steps: Add up nums[i] − min for every element.
pitfalls: Simulating the moves. With values up to 10⁹ apart this takes billions of steps.
Computing sum − n · min in 32-bit integers. The intermediate values overflow; sum the differences instead, or use 64-bit arithmetic.
Thinking the target is the maximum. Everyone keeps rising, so the final value is larger than the original maximum.

solutions.title: Sort, then measure gaps
solutions.idea: After sorting, the first element is the minimum. Every other element needs as many moves as its gap to it.

solutions.title: Sum of gaps to the minimum
solutions.idea: Raising all but one is the same as lowering one. Every element must be lowered to the minimum.

followups: Now a move adds or subtracts 1 from a single element. What is the minimum then? (Hint: the median.)
What if each move raises exactly n − 2 elements?
